significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that protein-model embedding geometry is ordered by catalytic chemistry after controlling for homology: “convergent same-mechanism enzymes will cluster in a mechanism subspace despite low sequence identity, while divergent homologs will separate,” with the abstraction strengthening in larger models. This is a form-(iii) ordering/scaling relation that predicts embedding behavior for additional convergent and divergent enzyme groups; it establishes a weighty representational phenomenon corresponding to scientific mechanisms, though not a causal mechanism producing a model behavior. Rives et al. (PNAS, 2021) established broad structure/function information in protein-language-model representations, while CLEAN (Yu et al., Science, 2023) uses learned embeddings for EC annotation, so determining whether transferable signal follows reaction chemistry rather than homology would materially constrain how remote-homology and orphan-enzyme predictions are interpreted. A verified-false result would rule out the stated homology-independent ordering and scaling account, though not every possible encoding of mechanism; true and false are distinguishable despite the loose word “partially,” and the topic-substitution check lowers the generic topic alone to the median rather than supporting this above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “mechanism-vs-homology discriminability score,” together with the claimed “mechanism subspace”; these provide a diagnostic for whether an embedding organizes enzymes by chemistry rather than ancestry. The diagnostic is primarily post hoc—the claim mentions “implications for annotating orphan enzymes” but does not itself assert prospective annotation accuracy or a pre-deployment failure forecast. After re-extraction on another protein model, however, the conclusion predicts the same ordering—same-mechanism convergent enzymes should be closer than divergent homologs—and predicts stronger separation at larger scale, so more than a model-specific search procedure survives recalibration across the asserted protein-language-model scope. Its immediate users would be protein-model and enzyme-annotation researchers rather than broad deployment practitioners; the topic-substitution check confirms that this reach comes from the quoted transferable relation and metric, not merely from the scientific domain.
